summary.headline: AESL Q2 FY27: total income up over 50%, EBITDA up ~67%, PAT up 145% as Energy Solutions earned strong merchant margins; smart meter deployment lagged.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as a strong quarter, with total income up over 50%, EBITDA up close to 67% and PAT up 145% year on year. Capex deployed in H1 reached about INR7,850 crore, described as an all-time high, with transmission capex guided to about INR14,000 crore for FY27. Energy Solutions revenue was over INR2,000 crore and EBITDA over INR800 crore in the quarter, helped by merchant market conditions that management said will not be repeated at that level. Smart meter installations were slower than expected in H1, which management attributed to consumer resistance and utility-specified installation scopes. Transmission commissioning in H1 was minimal, with ROW issues in Gujarat delaying Halvad and Navinal, and management still targets some FY27 commissioning.

financial_highlights.change: all-time high for a first half, as stated

financial_highlights.metric: Energy Solutions H1 long-term sale revenue

financial_highlights.value: about INR51,000 crore; net debt about INR41,000 crore

segments.name: Transmission
segments.commentary: Order book about INR87,000 crore after adding Vizag Pendurthi (data centres) and Satara (PSP-linked) interstate projects; management guided about INR8,000-9,000 crore of H2 FY27 capex against about INR14,000 crore for FY27, and INR18,000-19,000 crore for FY28.

segments.name: Distribution (AEML, MUL)
segments.commentary: Mumbai distribution losses fell to 4.29% in H1 FY27 while consumption rose more than 10%, per management.

segments.name: Smart Metering
segments.commentary: About 14.8 million meters delivered to date; H1 installations about 3.4 million. Plan for about 8-9 million meters in FY27, with the balance of about 4-4.5 million targeted in the following half year; the legacy order book completion is expected in 12-14 months.

segments.name: Energy Solutions platform (C&I)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue over INR2,000 crore and EBITDA over INR800 crore. Q2 volume about 14,583 MU, of which about 3,500 MU was merchant, 9,500 MU power trading on behalf of others and 1,500 MU power management services. Merchant EBITDA margin cited at INR1.70-2.00 per unit; agency trading at INR0.02-0.03 per unit.

guidance_outlook: Transmission capitalisation about INR15,000 crore guided earlier; management said no revision yet, and reassessment expected in the next six months. Capitalisation of about INR10,000 crore projected for FY28, with a lump jump after HVDC projects commission.
Transmission capex about INR14,000 crore for FY27 (H2 about INR8,000-9,000 crore), and about INR18,000-19,000 crore in FY28.
Smart meters: about 8-9 million installations in FY27; remainder of the order book to be completed in the next 12-14 months.
Energy Solutions: target of about 7,000-8,000 MW of combined supply and consumer tie-ups over 3-4 years; long-term margins of INR0.80-1.00 per unit on C&I/data centre PPAs.
Intellismart acquisition: completion expected within about one month, pending CCI approval.

Management guides to about 3,500 MU per quarter of merchant volume on current tie-ups, with seasonal variation; MSEDCL supply starts from end-February (1,000 MW), end-April (1,000 MW) and end-July (500 MW) of the following year.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex about INR7,850 crore; locked-in capex above INR100,000 crore to be delivered over 4-5 years, with asset base of about INR83,000 crore growing 1.3-1.4x.

Transmission commissioning: Khavda Phase 4 one element done; Khavda-Lakadia progressing; Halvad has about 50 locations pending due to ROW; WRSR at final commissioning stage with drone-based stringing; Navinal may slip to next year H1; Mahan Phase 1 this year, Phase 2 in Q1 next year.
Energy Solutions: about 4 GW of renewable and 3.5 GW of battery supply tie-ups; about 50% of the 2,500 MW MSEDCL PPA covered by sourcing.
Smart meter order book: about 60% delivered; auctions ongoing and the market seen as untapped for large volumes.
demand_pricing: Energy Solutions: merchant realisation about INR5.75 per unit on trading; agency trading margin INR0.02-0.03 per unit; merchant margin for the quarter INR1.70-2.00 per unit, which management said reflects market conditions in these two quarters and will not be sustained.
Consumer side: 2,500 MW MSEDCL PPA signed, 750 MW AEML PPA approved by regulator, about 400 MW of C&I clients, and multiple data centre discussions in advanced stage.

Transmission tender pipeline nationally about INR140,000 crore, tilted towards central (interstate) currently; new GEC-2 scheme is more focused on intrastate. Management said intrastate ROE is typically a little better than interstate.
Adani Green battery tie-up discussed on market benchmarks, not a fixed tariff; INR4.85 tariff referenced by an analyst was not confirmed as applicable.

qa_highlights.question: When will the Intellismart transaction close?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CCI approval is pending and expected soon; all utility approvals are secured, and completion is expected within about one month of CCI approval.

qa_highlights.question: Why was smart meter deployment slow in H1, and how will H2 pick up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited consumer resistance and utility-specified scopes (Maharashtra HT consumers first, Bihar tagging); with these resolved, pace is expected to rise significantly.

qa_highlights.question: Will Energy Solutions margins fall with the shift to long-term contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said long-term PPAs will yield steadier margins of about INR0.80-1.00 per unit versus the currently high merchant margins; volumes to rise to 7,000-8,000 MW over 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10 million smart meter target for FY27 still on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 target is about 8-9 million, with 4-4.5 million balance in the next half year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the transmission capitalisation target of about INR15,000 crore being revised?
qa_highlights.answer: Not for now; management is hopeful of completing WRSR, Halvad and Khavda Phase 4 this year and will reassess in the next six months.

qa_highlights.question: Does the MSEDCL contract require thermal supply, and who is the thermal partner?
qa_highlights.answer: No mandatory thermal component; management said it is exploring long-term thermal capacity from Adani Power or third parties, without locking in quantities.

risks_watch: Merchant margins in Energy Solutions were elevated in Q2 FY27; management acknowledged a possible softening until long-term PPA volumes start in Q4 FY27 and FY28.
Transmission commissioning delays in Gujarat due to ROW issues (Halvad, Navinal); H2 capex and FY27 capitalisation dependent on resolution.
Smart meter deployment pace and installation resistance; FY27 target reduced to about 8-9 million from the earlier 10 million.
Pending CCI approval for the Intellismart acquisition.
Curtailment risk on Adani Green supply: management said power not scheduled due to curtailment is the generator's responsibility, but the thermal sourcing for MSEDCL PPA remains unfixed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on capex deployment, the transmission pipeline and Energy Solutions growth, but cautious on near-term transmission commissioning and smart meter pace; several answers hedged on timing. Management was openly sceptical that the Q2 merchant margin would persist.
